t.6.79.1: Lakṣmaṇa, bearer of auspicious marks, his limbs drenched with blood, was filled with joy, having slain in battle him who had conquered Śakra.
t.6.79.2: Then that valiant one of great splendor, having turned back Jāmbavān and Hanumān and all those forest-dwellers as well...
t.6.79.4: Then Saumitri approached Rāma and, having saluted him, stood close beside his brother, as Indra's younger brother stands beside Śakra. Then the hero related the terrible slaying of Indrajit.
t.6.79.3: Then Lakṣmaṇa, leaning on Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanumān, came swiftly to the place where Sugrīva and Rāghava were.
t.6.79.5: Then Vibhīṣaṇa, delighted, reported to Rāma that the head of Rāvaṇi had been severed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.79.6: Seating the wounded Lakṣmaṇa on his lap and embracing him, kissing him on the head and caressing him again and again in his eagerness, that bull among men comforted Lakṣmaṇa and spoke these words to him.
t.6.79.7: A most auspicious deed has been accomplished by the doer of the difficult; today I have been made free of enemies. For Rāvaṇa, hearing that his son has been struck down, will surely march forth with a great array of forces.
t.6.79.8: That lord of the rākṣasas, hard to conquer, tormented by the slaying of his son, as he sallies forth, I shall surround with a mighty force and strike down.
t.6.79.9: O Lakṣmaṇa, with you as my protector, now that the conqueror of Śakra has been slain in battle today, neither Sītā nor the earth is hard for me to win.
t.6.79.10: Having comforted that brother of his and embraced him, Rāma the Rāghava, filled with joy, addressed Suṣeṇa and spoke these words.
t.6.79.11: This greatly wise Saumitri, devoted to his friends, is pierced with arrows; treat him in such a way that he becomes completely well. Let Saumitri, together with Vibhīṣaṇa, be quickly freed of the arrows.
t.6.79.12: Of the armies of bears and monkeys, those heroes who fight with trees, and whoever others are fighting here, pierced with arrows and wounded as well, let all of them be made whole and at ease by you with diligent effort.
t.6.79.13: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great-souled Suṣeṇa, leader of the monkey troops, gave Lakṣmaṇa the supreme herb through the nose.
t.6.79.14: Inhaling its fragrance, he was freed from the arrows; then he became free of pain as well, and his wounds were healed.
t.6.79.15: Then, at Rāghava's command, he gave medical treatment to their friends, headed by Vibhīṣaṇa, and to all the foremost of the monkeys.
t.6.79.16: Then Saumitri, the dart drawn out and his pain gone, returned to his natural state; there, in a moment, freed from his fever, he rejoiced.
t.6.79.17: Likewise Rāma, the lord of the monkeys, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Jāmbavān, the lord of the bears, together with the army, beholding Saumitri risen up free of illness, rejoiced with delight for a very long time.
t.6.79.18: The great-souled Dāśarathi praised the exceedingly difficult deed of Lakṣmaṇa. The chiefs of the monkey troops rejoiced in battle on hearing that Śakrajit had been struck down.
